claims.title: Rise of the Minoan palaces on Crete
claims.summary: The Minoan civilization built great palace complexes at Knossos and elsewhere on Crete, Europe's first advanced civilization, sustained by trade and a sophisticated artistic and administrative culture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-2000bce-rise-of-the-minoan-palaces-on-crete, claim TL:GRC:event:2000bce:rise-of-the-minoan-palaces-on-crete, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Flourishing of Mycenaean civilization
claims.summary: Fortified palace-citadels such as Mycenae and Pylos rose on the mainland, ruled by warrior elites who were the first attested Greek-speakers and traded across the eastern Mediterranean.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1600bce-flourishing-of-mycenaean-civilization, claim TL:GRC:event:1600bce:flourishing-of-mycenaean-civilization, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Linear B and Mycenaean control of Crete
claims.summary: Mycenaeans adapted Minoan script into Linear B to write an early form of Greek and extended their authority to Knossos, as Minoan power on Crete waned.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1450bce-linear-b-and-mycenaean-control-of-crete, claim TL:GRC:event:1450bce:linear-b-and-mycenaean-control-of-crete, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bronze Age collapse and the Greek Dark Ages
claims.summary: The Mycenaean palaces were destroyed and writing was lost in the wider Bronze Age collapse, ushering in centuries of decline known as the Greek Dark Ages.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1200bce-bronze-age-collapse-and-the-greek-dark-ages, claim TL:GRC:event:1200bce:bronze-age-collapse-and-the-greek-dark-ages, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Traditional first Olympic Games
claims.summary: Greek tradition dated the first Olympic Games to 776 BCE at Olympia, a panhellenic religious festival that became a shared marker of Greek identity and a basis for dating.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-776bce-traditional-first-olympic-games, claim TL:GRC:event:776bce:traditional-first-olympic-games, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cleisthenes founds Athenian democracy
claims.summary: The Athenian statesman Cleisthenes reorganized the citizens into ten tribes and established popular institutions of self-rule, the system later called democracy and regarded as the first in the world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-508bce-cleisthenes-founds-athenian-democracy, claim TL:GRC:event:508bce:cleisthenes-founds-athenian-democracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Marathon
claims.summary: Athenian hoplites defeated the first Persian invasion on the plain of Marathon, a landmark victory that became central to Athenian self-confidence and identity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-490bce-battle-of-marathon, claim TL:GRC:event:490bce:battle-of-marathon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Salamis
claims.summary: A Greek coalition fleet destroyed the navy of the Persian king Xerxes in the straits of Salamis, the decisive naval victory of the second Persian invasion; victory at Plataea in 479 BCE ended the threat.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-480bce-battle-of-salamis, claim TL:GRC:event:480bce:battle-of-salamis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Peloponnesian War
claims.summary: A protracted war between Athens and Sparta and their allies ended in Athens' defeat, exhausting the leading city-states and chronicled by the historian Thucydides.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-431bce-the-peloponnesian-war, claim TL:GRC:event:431bce:the-peloponnesian-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Chaeronea
claims.summary: Philip II of Macedon defeated an alliance of Greek city-states led by Athens and Thebes, ending the era of fully independent poleis and establishing Macedonian dominance over Greece.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-338bce-battle-of-chaeronea, claim TL:GRC:event:338bce:battle-of-chaeronea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alexander invades the Persian Empire
claims.summary: Alexander the Great crossed into Asia and began the campaign that, over a decade, toppled the Persian Empire and carried Greek arms and culture as far as India.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-334bce-alexander-invades-the-persian-empire, claim TL:GRC:event:334bce:alexander-invades-the-persian-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of Alexandria
claims.summary: Alexander founded Alexandria in Egypt, which became the greatest city of the Hellenistic world and a centre of Greek learning, home to its famous Library and Museum.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-331bce-foundation-of-alexandria, claim TL:GRC:event:331bce:foundation-of-alexandria, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Alexander and the Hellenistic kingdoms
claims.summary: Alexander died at Babylon, and his generals divided his empire into the Ptolemaic, Seleucid and Antigonid kingdoms, beginning the Hellenistic age of Greek-ruled states across the East.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-323bce-death-of-alexander-and-the-hellenistic-kingdoms, claim TL:GRC:event:323bce:death-of-alexander-and-the-hellenistic-kingdoms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rome sacks Corinth and conquers Greece
claims.summary: The Roman general Lucius Mummius destroyed Corinth and crushed the Achaean League, bringing Greece under Roman domination; it was later organized as the province of Achaea.

sources.label: Roman Greece (conquest and province of Achaea)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-146bce-rome-sacks-corinth-and-conquers-greece, claim TL:GRC:event:146bce:rome-sacks-corinth-and-conquers-greece, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of Constantinople
claims.summary: Constantine refounded Byzantium as Constantinople, the new capital that shifted the Roman Empire's centre eastward and became the heart of the Greek-speaking Byzantine world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-330-foundation-of-constantinople, claim TL:GRC:event:330:foundation-of-constantinople, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
claims.summary: Crusaders captured and plundered Constantinople, fragmenting Byzantine territory, including parts of Greece, among Latin and Greek rulers and gravely weakening the empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1204-fourth-crusade-sacks-constantinople, claim TL:GRC:event:1204:fourth-crusade-sacks-constantinople, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Constantinople
claims.summary: Ottoman forces under Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire and clearing the way for Ottoman rule over the Greek lands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1453-fall-of-constantinople, claim TL:GRC:event:1453:fall-of-constantinople, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman conquest of the Morea
claims.summary: The Ottomans completed their conquest of the Greek mainland with the fall of the Byzantine Despotate of the Morea, including Mystras, bringing the Greek lands under Ottoman rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1460-ottoman-conquest-of-the-morea, claim TL:GRC:event:1460:ottoman-conquest-of-the-morea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Outbreak of the Greek War of Independence
claims.summary: Revolution against Ottoman rule erupted across the Peloponnese and beyond, beginning the war that would create an independent Greek state and inspiring philhellenes across Europe.

sources.label: Greek Independence from the Ottoman Empire

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1821-outbreak-of-the-greek-war-of-independence, claim TL:GRC:event:1821:outbreak-of-the-greek-war-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Navarino
claims.summary: A combined British, French and Russian fleet destroyed the Ottoman-Egyptian navy at Navarino, a decisive intervention by the Great Powers that turned the war in Greece's favour.

sources.label: Greek Independence from the Ottoman Empire

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1827-battle-of-navarino, claim TL:GRC:event:1827:battle-of-navarino, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: London Protocol recognizes Greek independence
claims.summary: Britain, France and Russia signed the London Protocol declaring Greece an independent state, the first international act recognizing Greek sovereignty.

sources.label: 3 February 1830: Greece becomes a state (London Protocol)
sources.publisher: Greek News Agenda (General Secretariat for Media and Communication)

sources.label: Greek Independence from the Ottoman Empire

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1830-london-protocol-recognizes-greek-independence, claim TL:GRC:event:1830:london-protocol-recognizes-greek-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Constantinople and the Kingdom of Greece
claims.summary: The Ottoman sultan recognized Greek independence and the new state's frontiers in the Treaty of Constantinople; the Bavarian prince Otto was chosen as the first king of Greece.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1832-treaty-of-constantinople-and-the-kingdom-of, claim TL:GRC:event:1832:treaty-of-constantinople-and-the-kingdom-of, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Asia Minor Catastrophe
claims.summary: The Greco-Turkish War ended in the rout of Greek forces and the destruction of Smyrna in 1922; the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne mandated a population exchange that brought over a million refugees into Greece.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1922-asia-minor-catastrophe, claim TL:GRC:event:1922:asia-minor-catastrophe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Axis occupation of Greece
claims.summary: After resisting Italy in 1940, Greece was occupied by Germany, Italy and Bulgaria from 1941 to 1944, enduring a devastating famine and the deaths of hundreds of thousands of civilians.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1941-axis-occupation-of-greece, claim TL:GRC:event:1941:axis-occupation-of-greece, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Greek Civil War
claims.summary: Following liberation, a civil war between communist and government forces tore the country apart until 1949, an early conflict of the Cold War that left lasting political divisions.

sources.label: The Greek Civil War, 1944–1949
sources.publisher: The National WWII Museum, New Orleans

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1946-greek-civil-war, claim TL:GRC:event:1946:greek-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of the junta and the Third Hellenic Republic
claims.summary: After the collapse of the 1967–1974 military dictatorship, a referendum abolished the monarchy and established the current Greek parliamentary republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1974-fall-of-the-junta-and-the-third-hellenic, claim TL:GRC:event:1974:fall-of-the-junta-and-the-third-hellenic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Greece joins the European Communities
claims.summary: Greece became a member of the European Communities (later the European Union), anchoring its post-war democracy in European integration; it adopted the euro in 2001.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greece: Birthplace of democracy and philosophy, reborn as a modern nation through the War of Independence.", terralore.co/country/GRC/chronicle#ev-1981-greece-joins-the-european-communities, claim TL:GRC:event:1981:greece-joins-the-european-communities, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
